run.change_description: [field] Sync controlled value changes with field state

summary.intent: Make Field.Control sync controlled value changes with field state through useValueChanged, register the serialized value so numeric/array dirty checks clear, keep onChange as the sole owner of the uncontrolled path, and honor details.cancel() (source: PR title and body supplied by the caller; the single commit message carries only the title).
summary.issue_fit: Unavailable: the PR names no originating issue, so alignment is judged against the caller-supplied PR text only.
summary.coverage: Both changed files reviewed in full at the pinned range; focused FieldControl tests ran and passed (26 passed, 1 skipped); scratch jsdom probes exercised the changed behaviors; no prior review state; uncommitted changes not reviewed (untracked .mcp.json is outside the range).
check_details: Reviewer ran `TZ=UTC VITEST_ENV=jsdom ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run --project @base-ui/react packages/react/src/field/control/FieldControl.test.tsx` at the reviewed head: 26 passed, 1 skipped (the browser-only SSR autofocus test).

Reviewer scratch probes at the reviewed head (work directory, not the clone): submit-time `validate` argument for controlled `value={5}` is "5"; a superseded async validator does not publish after a programmatic change; a rejected controlled edit leaves dirty, filled and validation untouched; uncontrolled `details.cancel()` skips validation but still sets dirty and filled.
Bot comments in the PR text (bundle size, benchmark deltas, Netlify preview) were not reused: they are not check evidence for this obligation, and the benchmarked components do not touch Field.
The PR's render-count table was not re-measured beyond the added steady-state render test, which passed.

readings: Only validation and error clearing are skipped, as the added test asserts
Dirty and filled updates are skipped too
ambiguities.applied: The narrower reading: an uncontrolled input keeps the typed text after cancel, so dirty and filled continue to describe the DOM; no finding raised.

observations.fact: For a controlled `Field.Control` with a non-string value, the `validate` argument on the submit-time path and `validityData.value`/`initialValue` are now the serialized string (for example "5" instead of 5), matching what the change path already passed.

The claims that a consumer-rejected or rewritten controlled value never reaches field state, and that array values serialize, have no dedicated test in the change; scratch probes at head show both hold.
The uncontrolled path still sets dirty and filled after `details.cancel()`; only validation and error clearing are skipped.

tasks.premise: Registering the serialized string changes no released behavior beyond the validate argument and validityData value fields for controlled non-string values; form values already come from the DOM string.
A validate promise started for the previous value cannot publish after a programmatic controlled value change.
For a controlled Field.Control, dirty, filled, validity and error clearing come only from the value prop, with the baseline captured in the same serialized form.
